note: Made by the steps in TV_PICTURES.md: the chapter is split into sections that each carry one deep meaning ("sections"), 10 picture ideas are written for each, the top two for each picture are made and the better is chosen by eye (2026-11-22). Wide pictures only (1920x1088); the "tall" names are kept for the day tall pictures are switched back on. Each scene starts at the first word of its verse, or at its "from" words inside the verse. The important part of every picture sits in the upper two thirds, clear of the words. God is not pictured, Job is not portrayed as a biblical person but shown through ordinary people of today, and nothing violent is shown.
method: Second method, asked for by Obay on 2026-11-21 after the sentence-by-sentence pictures did not connect: (1) split the chapter into sections that each carry one deep meaning, written as one plain sentence; (2) write 10 different picture ideas for each section; (3) judge them: which shows the deep meaning most truly, then which a watcher understands at once while hearing the words, then which is most engaging; (4) make the top two for each picture slot as real pictures ("candidates") and choose by eye. A section has one or two pictures. What he said went wrong before: he could not tell why some pictures were there, could not connect them to the meaning, and some were too abstract.

sections.meaning: A human life is short and full of trouble: it blooms like a flower and withers, and passes like a shadow that does not stay.
ideas: A single wildflower in a green meadow, its head bowed and withered, its petals falling
An old man's weathered hand cradles one wilted flower, its petals dropping, fresh flowers blurred behind
A vase on a windowsill holding the same flower fresh, full-blown and dried brown side by side
A person's shadow slides across a sunlit wall, the person out of sight
A cloud's shadow races across a hillside and is gone
A dandelion clock blowing apart in the wind
A man's long evening shadow stretches over a field and fades as the sun drops
A newborn's tiny hand and an old man's hand side by side
A morning-glory open at dawn and closed and shrivelled by evening
Petals blown off a blossoming tree in a sudden gust

sections.meaning: Why fix a judging eye on so frail and fleeting a creature, who cannot make himself clean and whose days are already counted out? Look away and let him rest until his day's work is done.
ideas: A frail old man stands small and alone in a vast dark courtroom under one hard beam of light, the high judge's bench empty above him
A small moth caught in a searchlight's beam at night
A man squints under an interrogation lamp at a bare table
Muddy water poured from a jug comes out muddy in the clear glass
Hands scrubbing at a stain on a white shirt that will not come out
A tired day labourer sits resting against the end post of a vineyard row at sunset, his full crate beside him
A builder sits on a low wall at a finished site at dusk, hard hat beside him, eyes closed
A labourer walks home at dusk with his tools on his shoulder
An hourglass with the last sand running out on a workbench
A field fence at the edge of the world that no one can pass

sections.meaning: A tree has hope: cut down to an old dead stump, at the scent of water it sprouts again.
ideas: An old grey stump in a clearing ringed with strong young green shoots
A dead stump in dry cracked ground; a thin stream has just reached it and fresh leafy shoots spring up
Rain falling on a sawn stump where one bright green shoot rises
A gardener pours water at the foot of a stump that has begun to bud
A sawn log end with a single new leaf on it
A felled orchard with one stump in blossom
A stump half-buried in dust with buds bursting from its bark
Roots of an old stump reaching for a spring of water
A row of stumps after logging, one sprouting thick green branches
A child kneeling to look at a shoot growing out of a stump

sections.meaning: But a man dies and is gone: like water drained away from a lake, he lies down and does not rise again.
ideas: A dried-up lake bed of cracked mud with an old rowboat stranded far from any water
A dry riverbed under a stone bridge, only cracked mud and stones
An empty armchair by a window, his reading glasses on a closed book and his cardigan over the arm
A neatly made empty bed with a pair of slippers beside it
A wooden jetty running out over a lake that has dried away
A coat and hat hanging on a hook in an empty hall
Footprints in the sand that simply stop
A dry fountain in an empty square
An empty porch rocking chair at evening
A drained swimming pool full of dead leaves

sections.meaning: Job longs for hope beyond death: to be hidden until God's anger passes, waiting like a soldier for his relief, and then called back by a God who longs for him and covers his sin.
ideas: A lone night watchman at a remote post keeps watch through the night, looking toward the first light where his relief will come
A man shelters in a hollow in the rocks while a storm rages outside, looking out for it to pass
A seed lying in dark soil under snow while spring light reaches the surface
A father, seen from behind at the farmhouse door at dusk, calls out across the fields, and far off his grown son turns, raises his hand and starts for home
A father kneels with open arms as a small child runs to him at his call
A craftsman's hands hold a carved wooden bird he made long ago
A trowel smooths fresh plaster over a deep crack in a wall until the crack is gone
A canvas bag of stones is tied shut and sealed
The tide washes dark marks out of the sand
A slate wiped clean

sections.meaning: But as mountains crumble and water wears stones away, so God wears down a man's hope; he is sent away and never knows how his children fare, feeling only his own pain.
ideas: A sea cliff crumbling, a great slab of rock and earth sliding down into the surging waves
A boulder in a mountain stream worn smooth and hollowed by the water running over it
A sandcastle melting as a wave washes over it
A rockfall that has blocked a mountain road
Rain washing the soil off a hillside field into a brown flood
At an awards ceremony a young man is applauded on stage while one front-row seat stays empty, an old man's cap on it
An old man seen from behind walks away alone down a long country road into evening mist
An old man's photograph on a mantel while his grown children celebrate in the room
A son's wedding with one empty chair reserved
An old man alone at a window, his face turned away, while the street outside goes on without him

candidates.prompt: A single wildflower in a green summer meadow, close up. Its head is bowed and withered, its petals curled brown and falling away one by one onto the grass, while the meadow round it is still fresh and green. Soft clear afternoon light.

A close view of an old man's weathered hand cradling one wilted flower on its stem, its head drooping and its petals dropping from it. Behind, softly out of focus, a garden of fresh flowers in bloom. Soft clear daylight.

A vast, dark, wood-panelled modern courtroom. Far below the empty raised judge's bench, a frail grey-haired man in a plain shirt stands small and alone in the middle of the floor, caught in one hard bright beam of light from above. No judge, no other people; the high bench towers over him, empty.
On a plain wooden kitchen table, a jug of muddy brown water is being poured into a clean clear drinking glass, and the water filling the glass is just as muddy and brown. Bright window light.

At sunset at the end of a long vineyard row, a tired day labourer in work clothes sits on the ground resting with his back against the last post, eyes closed, his hat in his lap. A full crate of picked grapes stands beside him. The day's work is done and the light is golden and calm.

At dusk on a finished building site, a tired labourer sits resting on a low brick wall, his hard hat and gloves beside him, his eyes closed and his shoulders loose. The work of the day is done. Soft evening light.

An old grey weathered tree stump in a sunny woodland clearing, cut down long ago, cracked and dead on top. All round its rim strong young green shoots and leafy branches are springing up, fresh and bright. Clear morning light.

A dead grey tree stump stands in dry cracked earth. A thin trickle of fresh water has just run across the dry ground and reached its roots, and bright new green buds and small leafy branches are bursting out of the old stump. Clear daylight.

A wide lake bed that has dried up completely: a plain of cracked grey mud stretching to the far hills, with the old shoreline marked on the banks. In the middle an old wooden rowboat lies stranded on the cracked mud, far from any water. Hazy pale daylight.

A quiet living room in soft daylight. By the window stands an empty worn armchair. On the side table next to it lie a pair of reading glasses folded on a closed book, and a grey cardigan hangs over the arm of the chair. The room is still and no one is there.

At a lonely remote lookout post on a hilltop, a single night watchman in a plain dark jacket stands at the rail keeping watch, seen from the side. It is the end of a long night, and he is looking toward the far horizon where the first pale light of dawn is beginning, waiting for his relief to come up the empty road.

A man sits sheltering inside a deep hollow in a rock face while a fierce storm of rain and wind sweeps the valley outside. He is safe and dry in the dark of the hollow, looking out, waiting for the storm to pass. Far off, the clouds are beginning to break.

At dusk a father, seen from behind, stands in the lit doorway of a farmhouse with one hand cupped to his mouth, calling out across the fields. Far off across the field his grown son has turned toward the house and raised his hand in answer, and is starting back toward home. Warm light from the doorway.

A close view of a plasterer's hands with a steel trowel smoothing fresh white plaster over a long deep crack in an old wall. On one side the crack is still open and dark; where the trowel has passed it is gone, covered with smooth clean plaster. Clear daylight.

A tall sea cliff of earth and rock is crumbling into the ocean: a great slab of rock and soil is breaking away and sliding down into the surging grey waves below, which have worn the foot of the cliff hollow. Overcast daylight.

In a mountain stream, a large boulder has been worn smooth and hollowed into deep curves by the water rushing over it year after year; the current runs over it, carrying away sand and earth. Clear daylight.
On a beach a carefully built sandcastle is collapsing as a wave washes over it, its towers slumping and melting into the water. Clear daylight.

In a bright school hall during an awards ceremony, a young man in a suit stands on the stage holding up an award while the audience applauds. Seen from the side aisle at the height of the seats, the front row runs across the middle of the picture, and in its centre one chair is empty, with an old man's flat cap and folded jacket laid on it. No writing or banners anywhere.
An old man, seen from behind, walks away alone down a long straight empty country road into the evening mist, small and growing faint, his shoulders bowed. The road and fields fade into the grey.

A close view at eye level of a jug of muddy brown water being poured into a clean clear drinking glass that stands on a high wooden shelf by a bright window, and the water filling the glass is just as muddy and brown as what is in the jug. The glass and the pouring stream are in the upper middle of the picture; below them is only the plain wood of the shelf front in soft shadow. Bright window light.

At dusk a father, seen from behind, stands in the lit doorway of a farmhouse with both hands cupped round his mouth, plainly calling out loud across the fields. Far off across the field his grown son has turned toward the house and lifted his arm high in answer, and is starting back toward home. Warm light from the doorway. The father's head and cupped hands and the distant son are in the upper half of the picture.
